question.text: Under the existing SEBI (AIF) Regulations, is appointing a custodian mandatory for all AIFs?

answer.text: Only mandatory for Category III AIFs dealing in listed securities
Only mandatory if corpus exceeds INR 500 crore
Mandatory for all AIFs; each scheme can have a different custodian to segregate assets and liabilities
Optional; trustees can perform custodial functions internally

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 357, appointing a custodian is mandatory for all AIFs, and each scheme can have a different custodian to segregate the assets and liabilities of that scheme. Page 358 cites Regulation 20(11), which requires sponsors/managers of AIFs to appoint a custodian for safekeeping of securities, and notes that the appointment must be in place before the first investment. The Trap: The Category III-only or above-INR 500 crore options reflect outdated thresholds; the mandatory requirement now applies across all AIFs. Trustees cannot substitute for the custodian function. Note: The mandatory custodian rule, scheme-level segregation, and Regulation 20(11) language are grounded in pages 357-358. Historical threshold details and SLA negotiation commentary should be separately sourced before being relied upon.
